clue.text: Claim — why it is thrown out as a fantasy

indicators.note: thrown out suggests letters tossed about and landing in a new order, so the four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's claim is dismissed as pure fantasy, the reasons for rejecting it being asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' looks like rejection of the claim, but it signals that CLAIMWHYITIS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe fanciful, capricious imagination rather than sober reality.

clue.text: Our present state

parts.note: read as the condition we are all in now, and also as the British system of state provision that the nation then enjoyed

explanation.surface: A comment on the condition of the nation today.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the 'welfare state', newly founded in postwar Britain, and on a present state of well-being.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-being is our current condition, and the postwar British system of public benefits was called the state of that name.

clue.text: Direction of X-rays for patients here

definitions.text: Direction of X-rays for patients here

parts.words: Direction of X-rays for patients here
parts.note: X-rays travel into the body, and hospital patients who are admitted lie on hospital wards, so the phrase splits in two

explanation.surface: A hospital sign directing patients to the radiography department.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN WARDS: that is where in-patients are, while the whole word is the way X-rays go, into the body.
explanation.definitionFit: X-rays pass toward the inside of the body, and hospital patients lie in the wards.

clue.text: Silhouettes — one of these at the fair.?

definitions.text: Silhouettes — one of these at the fair

parts.words: Silhouettes — one of these at the fair
parts.note: a silhouette shows a person in profile, displaying one flank of the face, and a fairground has minor attractions alongside the main event

explanation.surface: A silhouette-cutter's stall is one of the attractions at a fairground.
explanation.walkthrough: Silhouettes literally show sides (profiles), and silhouette-cutting was a familiar fairground stall.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor fairground attractions are called this, and a profile cut in black paper literally displays a flank of the face.

clue.text: Described as .a knavish lad by Puck

definitions.text: Described as .a knavish lad by Puck

parts.words: Described as .a knavish lad by Puck
parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream the sprite Puck calls the god of love a knavish lad who makes poor females mad

explanation.surface: A literary quotation from Shakespeare's mischievous sprite.
explanation.walkthrough: Puck, in A Midsummer Night's Dream (Act 3), says the god of love is a knavish lad, thus to make poor females mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Puck uses these words of the Roman god of love, the boy archer.

clue.text: Watch' with concern

definitions.meaning: a watch is a sentry or a careful vigil
a concern is one's own business, as in 'that's your own affair'

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on things anxiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's your look-out' means that is your own concern or responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry keeping vigil is one sense; one's own business or responsibility, as in 'that's your affair', is the other.

clue.text: Indulge in temporary duplicity ?

parts.note: temporary hints at a period, and duplicity at doubleness, so the phrase also reads as a pair and a period

explanation.surface: Be unfaithful to a partner for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Duplicity is doubleness (two) and temporary relates to time, while the whole means to deceive a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheating on a partner is a deceit, and the word literally joins a pair with a period.

clue.text: Employer parts with the best works

parts.note: a master is one who employs servants or workmen
pieces are parts or portions of something

explanation.surface: A boss's components join with the finest products of a workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: The finest creations of an artist or craftsman are called this, originally the work that proved a craftsman's skill.

clue.text: Nothing's settled, granted

definitions.meaning: if no debt is paid, everything is still owing, read as two words

explanation.surface: Even though no bill has been paid, permission has been given.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into ALL OWED: when nothing's settled, everything is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Permitted is a synonym; split into two words it describes a state where every debt remains unpaid.

clue.text: Partisans-leader of them meeting the Head

parts.note: the Provos were the Provisional IRA, guerrilla fighters

indicators.note: leader of picks the opening letter of the word them

explanation.surface: The chief of a band of guerrillas has a meeting with the headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: PROVOS is a familiar name for members of the Provisional IRA; 'meeting the' joins them to the opening of 'them'.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal of certain colleges, and the chief magistrate of a Scottish town, carries this title.

clue.text: Spots where the high boys gather in pubs ?

definitions.text: Spots where the high boys gather in pubs

parts.words: Spots where the high boys gather in pubs
parts.note: high suggests drunk, and drinkers cluster in the nooks of a bar, while spots means difficult predicaments

explanation.surface: Describes the nooks of a bar where tipsy lads congregate.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight means drunk, so drunk lads in pub corners are in 'tight corners', which are awkward predicaments.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward predicaments are this, and tipsy drinkers huddle in the angles of a bar.

clue.text: Nuts are loose in these boilers

indicators.note: loose suggests the letters coming free and resettling in a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that the bolts on some heating equipment have worked free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' signals rearranging NUTSARE; 'Nuts' looks like hardware.
explanation.definitionFit: These are large heated vessels for boiling water for a beverage in canteens.

clue.text: Condemning performance — out of order

indicators.note: out of here means the order sits with the performance wrapped around its outside

parts.note: doing is the act of performing something
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A harsh review condemns a performance as quite improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' reads as a verdict on the show, but 'out of' is the container signal; OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To sentence or consign someone to a dire fate is to condemn them.

clue.text: Connexions of Macgillicuddy with Edinburgh ?

parts.note: Macgillicuddy's mountain range in Kerry shares a word with Edinburgh's nickname Auld Reekie, and the plural verb also means smells

explanation.surface: A genealogical query about an Irish clan's links with the Scottish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Macgillicuddy's Reeks are mountains in County Kerry, Ireland, and Edinburgh is nicknamed Auld Reekie for its smoky air.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish mountain range and the Scottish city's nickname share this word, which also means stinks.

clue.text: The way of the City is by no means modern

definitions.text: The way of the City is by no means modern

parts.words: The way of the City is by no means modern
parts.note: the way is a road in the City of London, and by no means modern describes it as ancient

explanation.surface: A remark that the City of London's customs are far from up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: OLD STREET is a London road near the City, the financial district; 'way' looks like a manner but is a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A road running into the City of London bears this name, which literally describes an ancient thoroughfare.

clue.text: Inner discomfort, said Pepys, is wrong .

indicators.note: is wrong suggests the letters are not in their proper order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: The diarist Samuel Pepys complains of a stomach ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wrong' tells you to rearrange SAIDPEPYS; Pepys the diarist is a fitting speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestion is a discomfort felt inside, in the stomach.

clue.text: Raises positions of batsmen

definitions.meaning: in cricket, the crease is the line where a batsman stands, so being in it is a safe position

explanation.surface: A promotion boosts the batting order of a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the marked line a batsman stands behind; split the answer as IN CREASES.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise is to make greater; split in two, it places cricket batsmen at their marked lines.

clue.text: Dock brief trouble

parts.note: curt means brief or short
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A short legal brief in the dock causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock brief' is a legal term (a barrister engaged in court by a prisoner in the dock), but 'Dock' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock is to cut short, just as a tail is cut.

clue.text: Rubs out notes on maps

parts.note: E and F are two musical notes
map is slang for face, so maps are faces

explanation.surface: Someone erases annotations written on charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'map' is old slang for a face; 'on' places the notes before the faces in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase writing is to wipe it from the surface.

clue.text: Follow with success (hidden)

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow closely
a go is a success, as in make a go of it

explanation.surface: Tail someone successfully while staying out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'lie doggo' is to stay quiet and out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase lie low and keep quiet uses this word to mean concealed.

clue.text: A flop gone bad in the heat

parts.note: a dud is a flop or failure

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of gone have gone off and are disordered

explanation.surface: A failed scheme turns sour in the heat of the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' is the anagram signal for the four letters of 'gone' only; 'in the' is a link to the definition, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentful anger, as in 'high dudgeon', is a heated emotion.

clue.text: Girl, one to reduce with turpentine

parts.note: gal is a colloquial girl
I is the Roman numeral for one
to pot is to abridge, as in a potted history

explanation.surface: A girl uses turpentine to cut down something.
explanation.walkthrough: A potted account is a reduced or condensed one.
explanation.definitionFit: A crude turpentine is the resin scraped from pine trees, a kind of turpentine.

clue.text: Vehicle needs change of fuel, and such a driver

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: change of tells you to alter the order of the letters of fuel

explanation.surface: A motorist who switches fuels is a cautious one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' is the anagram signal; the definition leans on the whole clue, picturing the motorist in question.
explanation.definitionFit: A cautious driver, taking pains to avoid danger, is described this way.

clue.text: Hen's bed

definitions.meaning: a hen is one that lays eggs
a bed is a stratum of rock or soil

explanation.surface: Where a chicken roosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hen's' reads as 'hen is', so a hen is a layer; a bed of rock is a layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen is a bird that produces eggs, and a geological bed is a stratum.

clue.text: Heathen deity-in eternity a mere phantom

indicators.note: in places the heathen deity inside the word for eternity

parts.note: an eon is an age or eternity
an idol is a heathen god

explanation.surface: A pagan god lasting forever turns out to be only a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre or insubstantial image is called this, from Greek for an apparition.

clue.text: Yachts adrift-round the river to be precise

indicators.note: round places the rearranged yachts around the river
adrift suggests the yacht letters floating out of position

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Boats drifting around a river need precise navigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adrift' rearranges YACHTS, and 'round' puts it around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiffly formal and prim is starchy, the way a person fussy about details can be.

clue.text: A beam for this kind of ear-ring

definitions.meaning: a heavy wooden beam supports railway lines
a small ring worn to keep a pierced earlobe open

explanation.surface: A girder suitable for making an unusual earring.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeper is a plain ring worn to stop a newly pierced hole closing; a railway sleeper is a beam under the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway track rests on these timbers, and a plain stud worn to keep a pierced lobe open has the same name.

clue.text: Wolseley so entirely satisfactory!

parts.note: all means entirely, wholly
Sir Garnet Wolseley was a Victorian British general famed for efficient campaigns

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising the Victorian general Wolseley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All Sir Garnet' was Victorian slang for everything in order, after the efficient General Sir Garnet Wolseley.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian expression meant everything was in order, after a general known for efficiency.
